subject: Ops signal brief: wins, pressures & leadership asks
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Ops signal brief: wins, pressures & leadership asks

Team —

Quick weekly signal from the ops desk and QBR prep for Acme (QBR scheduled 6/18). Keeping this tight: three wins, three pressures/risks, and three leadership asks. Attachment: QBR_onepager_v3.pdf (one-pager for execs).

WINS
- Completed prefix-cache rollout for the high-volume search workload; 9% reduction in P90 latency across the cluster.
- Demo with Acme success: pilot users validated end-to-end ingest and embeddings; technical pilot now in week 3.
- Billing reconciliation: cleared discrepancy for May usage; finance confirmed corrected invoice sent.

PRESSURES / RISKS
- SLA exception request: Acme is pushing for a 99.99% p95 latency SLA for a narrow set of routes. Current baseline at their volume would require reserved capacity + autoscale changes. See SLA_exception_request.docx.
- GPU spot churn in us-west causing transient node pressure (expected higher through next fortnight). Could bump latency during peak windows.
- Eval regression: our recent quantization profile for Llama-2-XXL shows small but measurable hallucination increase on one of Acme's prompt sets. Research is on a mitigation branch but not yet validated.

LEADERSHIP ASKS
1) Approve a short-term SLA exception/commit for Acme for a 3-month window (covers autoscale and reserved capacity costs). Requesting a thumbs-up by EOD Tue so we can present a committed plan on the 6/18 QBR.
2) Allocate a small incident credit ($8k) to cover Acme's observed spikes in May while we finish cache rollout (finance + legal pre-approved range).
3) Prioritize research validation on the quantization regression — need an expedited test matrix and one dedicated engineer for 2 weeks.

Notes: Marissa — I'll loop CS into the external comms after we confirm the SLA wording. Vivek/Markus — if we green-light a 3-month exception, I propose a canary in us-west with reserved pool + prewarmed workers.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR_onepager_v3.pdf (one-page summary), SLA_exception_request.docx (draft request)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops signal brief: wins, pressures & leadership asks

Thanks, Grace — good concise summary. Quick follow-ups: 

- On the SLA exception, can you quantify incremental monthly run-rate for the reserved pool (ballpark $)? We should put that into the finance ask.
- On spot churn: any logs showing correlation to specific instance families? If it's limited to one family we can add anti-affinity and reduce churn.

If you can drop a one-line cost delta for the reserved pool, I can escalate to finance today.

-Vivek

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Amanda Li <amanda@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Acme QBR prep: draft ask and one-pager

Amanda —

Following our pilot demos, attaching a one-pager (QBR_onepager_v3.pdf) for the upcoming customer QBR on 6/18. Two brief items I want to confirm with you ahead of the meeting: 

1) SLA window: we've proposed a 3-month targeted SLA exception for the specific low-latency routes you flagged while we scale reserved capacity and finish the cache rollout. This is a temporary commitment to ensure product stability at scale — see attached SLA_exception_request.docx for the proposed wording and the fallback policy.
2) Acceptance plan: we will run a canary in us-west for 48 hours before the comms and provide telemetry dashboards and a short post-canary readout.

Can you confirm: are you comfortable with a 3-month exception and a canary runway? If yes, I'll finalize the wording and share a DocuSign link for the SLA amendment before the QBR.

Thanks,
Grace

Attachments: QBR_onepager_v3.pdf, SLA_exception_request.docx
From: Amanda Li <amanda@acme.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme QBR prep: draft ask and one-pager

Grace —

Thanks for the one-pager and the clear path. We are agreeable to the 3-month exception provided: 
- We receive the post-canary telemetry dashboard and a week-of QBR runbook that lists fallback steps.
- The SLA amendment has a clear rollback clause if the canary does not meet agreed P95 targets.

If you can send the DocuSign and the canary runbook by Monday EOD (6/14), we will review with our CISO and be ready for a final decision during the 6/18 QBR.

—Amanda
Amanda Li
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ops signal brief: wins, pressures & leadership asks — updates + ask for decisions

Team — quick update after Acme ack and internal follow-ups: 

1) Cost delta: Finance provided an estimate for the reserved pool to meet Acme's p95 target — incremental run-rate ~ $14k/month for the reserved capacity and prewarmed workers (this includes autoscale headroom). Vivek, marking this in the ask.

2) Spot churn: infra confirmed churn localized to g5-family instances; plan to add anti-affinity and set a conservative drain threshold. Expected reduction in transient impact by next week.

3) Quantization regression: Research proposes a narrow rollback to the previous quant profile for Acme's routes during the 3-month exception window; that will be validated in the canary. We will not roll this to other customers without sign-off.

Leadership decisions requested: 
- Approve the 3-month SLA exception and the $14k/month reserved pool (we'll bill Acme per the amendment; Redwood will absorb the prewarm delta for month 1 to ease the transition).
- Approve the $8k incident credit to be issued in June.
- Approve allocation of one dedicated engineer (2 weeks) for the quantization validation during the canary.

If I don't hear an objection by Mon 6/15 11:00am PT, I'll treat this as approved and proceed to finalize the DocuSign and runbook.

Thanks — GRACE
Grace O'Connor
Director of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
